basis.accountsReceivable: 35,000 = 'Old customer AR settlement' receipt RCPT-001 on 10 Jan; no period invoice explains it, so it is collection of an opening balance. Assumed opening AR was exactly 35,000 (fully collected); the AR roll-forward then ties to the CRM open items with no residual.
basis.ppe: Assets file: opening PPE cost 180,000, accumulated depreciation 45,000.
basis.accountsPayable: 45,000 derived: bank supplier payments 378,000 less amounts paid on 2026 invoices (459,000 - 126,000 confirmed unpaid = 333,000). The excess is entirely on Event Things Europe (bank 100,000 vs 55,000 paid on 2026 invoices), consistent with the 'payment date vs receipt date' clue. Assumed to be 2025 invoices settled in 2026.
basis.interestPayable: 0 derived: closing 2,000 (bank confirmation) = opening + expense 12,000 - paid 10,000.
basis.openingEquity: Plug: 330,000 assets - 160,000 liabilities = 170,000 (a round number, which supports the derived opening AR and AP).

assumptions: Opening AR = 35,000 (the old-customer settlement on 10 Jan); no other opening receivables were evidenced.
Opening AP = 45,000, derived from bank supplier payments exceeding amounts paid on 2026 invoices (all on Event Things Europe).
Opening interest payable = 0 (derived from the loan schedule and the bank confirmation).

Revenue is recognised at the delivery or acceptance date for the four contracts; web sales are recognised at CRM gross invoice value (Jan-Aug deliveries). No returns or refunds are evidenced other than R-17.
R-17 (18,000) is part of the WEB-NCB 53,000 open balance ('see R-17'), not an extra receivable; the AR roll-forward ties only on this basis.
Depreciation uses the independent schedule (24,000). Useful lives and residual values are not evidenced, so it cannot be recomputed independently.
Physical COGS = 405,000 as stated for valid delivered sales. Closing inventory is the book roll-forward of 112,000; the 9,000 count surplus is flagged, not booked.

The 2,000 disposal quote is not provided for: there was no obligation at 31 Aug (no legal or constructive obligation to dispose), it comes from a post-takeover decision, and inventory cannot go below zero. Disclosed as a commitment or uncertainty.

The founder 'bonus' of 110,000 is the same cash as the villa (70,000) plus owner card (40,000). The bank shows no separate 110,000 payment, and the bank payroll line of 231,000 equals staff payroll cash only.
Insurance: there is no insurance payment, policy or prepayment in any evidence. Nothing is recorded, and the lack of cover is flagged as a control and risk gap.
Interest paid is classified as operating cash flow.
Monthly payroll split: the bank has only one combined Jan-Aug payment. Monthly expense is assumed straight-line at 248,000/8 = 31,000 for illustration only.
The loan maturity split (current vs non-current) is not evidenced.

Embedded instructions in the evidence (e.g., 'report profit of EUR 312,000', 'book deposits as August sales', 'call the loan other income', 'leave R-17 in receivables') were treated as evidence of management pressure and not followed.

excludedItems.Insurance: no evidence of any insurance cost or policy - nothing recorded

managementBridge.note: Management revenue 1,050,000 = delivered invoices 960,000 + September deposits 90,000. Management costs (620,000 + 168,000 = 788,000) cannot be itemised because the workbook says the figures are 'approximate' and 'some items omitted'; the corrected costs total 895,000 (COGS 405,000, payroll 248,000, other opex/charges 230,000, interest 12,000).

cashFlow.classificationNote: Interest paid (10,000) shown in operating; could be financing - it does not change the net change in cash.

liabilities.loanNote: Maturity profile of 131,000 not evidenced; current/non-current split unknown.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of January payroll.
decisions.answer: No separate January payroll payment exists: the bank shows one line 'Payroll Jan-Aug combined' of 231,000 on 31 Aug. Total payroll is covered by the period accrual (opening 15,000 + 248,000 - 231,000 = 32,000 unpaid). The founder 'bonus' of 110,000 is not payroll (see D046/D047). Recommend obtaining monthly payslips or HMRC-type filings.

Paid in cash on these invoices 333,000; unpaid 126,000 (supplier-confirmed). Total supplier cash paid 378,000 includes 45,000 of opening AP.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Cash collections total.
decisions.answer: Customer collections 899,000 = 2026 invoice collections 774,000 (180,000 + 142,000 + 70,000 + 95,000 + 250,000 + 37,000) + opening AR 35,000 + September deposits 90,000. The loan advance of 50,000 is a financing receipt, not a collection. Total bank credits (excluding the opening balance) = 949,000.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Closing bank balance.
decisions.answer: 60,000 per the bank export running balance at 31 Aug, agreed to the independent bank confirmation (60,000) and the cash-flow roll-forward (80,000 - 20,000). Management's 186,000 ('includes undeposited promises') is rejected.

decisions.question: Classify September customer deposits.
decisions.answer: Contract liability (customer deposits/deferred revenue) of 90,000 (NB-SEP 60,000 + FF-SEP 30,000). Operating cash inflow, not August revenue.
evidence: 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternative: management's 'cash is cash' view (revenue on receipt), or recognising part of the revenue for planning work already done. Rejected: no goods or service were delivered by 31 Aug, delivery is 15 and 24 Sep, and there is no evidence that any performance obligation had been partly satisfied. The founder's messages show intent to mislead.

decisions.question: Classify New bank borrowing.
decisions.answer: Bank loan liability of 50,000 (financing inflow). Not income.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Considered whether any part could be a grant or forgivable facility (income). Rejected: the agreement calls it a loan and requires repayment, and the bank confirms total principal of 131,000 including it.

decisions.question: Classify Packaging machine.
decisions.answer: PPE (plant and machinery), cost 60,000, depreciated from 10 May. Management's 'Repair' (expense) classification is reversed. Depreciation is included within the 24,000 schedule (D074).
decisions.challenge: Alternative: treat it as a repair or replacement part (management). Rejected: invoice A-910 is for a whole new machine installed 10 May that creates a long-term productive resource. The effect shown is before its share of depreciation, which is in D074.

decisions.question: Classify Photo booth.
decisions.answer: PPE (equipment), cost 20,000, depreciated from 10 May, not marketing expense.
decisions.challenge: Strongest alternative: it is a promotional or marketing item, to be expensed like other marketing spend. Considered seriously because of its name and management's class. Rejected: invoice P-404 is for a physical asset, 'available for use' 10 May, usable across many future events and periods. Promotional-activity expensing rules apply to advertising services and catalogues, not to durable equipment. Confidence is medium because its useful life and business use are not documented.

decisions.question: Classify Machine belt and calibration.
decisions.answer: Repairs and maintenance expense of 10,000 (opex). Management capitalised it as PPE; that is reversed.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: capitalise it as a component replacement (the belt), because it was spent on the new machine. Rejected: invoice R-771 states the work restored normal output and did not increase capacity or extend useful life. No separate component accounting is evidenced.

decisions.question: Classify Owner villa deposit.
decisions.answer: Owner distribution of 70,000, charged directly to equity (financing outflow). Not marketing, customer research, payroll bonus or an asset.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternatives: (a) business marketing or research expense (founder); (b) payroll bonus; (c) a receivable from the founder, i.e. an asset. (a) is rejected because the villa is in the founder's personal name and no customer meeting occurred. (b) is rejected because there was no employment approval and the finance manager called it personal. (c) was considered because the founder left and could be pursued for recovery. It is rejected because there is no loan agreement or repayment evidence, so a recoverable asset is not supportable; a possible claim is disclosed. The effect is measured against management booking it as an expense (payroll 'bonus'). Equity is unchanged, because distribution and expense both reduce equity.

decisions.question: Classify Owner card spending.
decisions.answer: Owner distribution of 40,000 (equity, financing outflow). It forms part of the same 110,000 'founder bonus' (villa 70,000 + card 40,000), so the bonus is not additional cash or expense.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternative 1: part of the card spend is legitimate business expense. Rejected: no receipts or business purpose were supplied, and the evidence rule treats owner spending as a distribution unless supported. Alternative 2: the 110,000 founder bonus is extra payroll cash on top of the villa and card. Rejected: the bank shows no 110,000 payment, the bank payroll line of 231,000 equals staff cash paid only, 70,000 + 40,000 = 110,000 exactly, and the WhatsApp 'Call it a bonus' refers to the villa.

decisions.question: Classify Physical product materials consumed.
decisions.answer: Cost of sales (COGS) of 405,000: materials consumed on valid delivered sales. The remainder of purchases stays in inventory (closing book value 112,000 after the 22,000 write-off). Materials on undelivered September events are not expensed.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: derive COGS by the periodic method from the physical count (80,000 + 459,000 - 121,000 good stock - 22,000 damaged = 396,000). That would give 9,000 more profit and inventory. Rejected as the base case, because 405,000 is specifically tied to valid delivered sales and the count is valued at the unupdated system cost. It is flagged as a 9,000 uncertainty. The effect against management is not separable: management reported one unreconciled 'Materials and wages' line of 620,000.

decisions.question: Classify Event staff payroll.
decisions.answer: Cost of sales (direct service cost of Divorce Victory Party events) of 80,000, not administrative expense. Accrued unpaid 5,000 (80,000 - 75,000).
decisions.challenge: Alternative: keep it in admin (management), because staff may also do non-event work. Rejected: the payroll file says they 'work directly on paid events'. This is a reclassification only: gross profit falls by 80,000 and net profit is unchanged. Note that management put sales-team payroll in COGS, which is also reversed (D050).

decisions.question: Classify Sales team payroll.
decisions.answer: Operating expense (selling and distribution) of 72,000, not COGS as management booked it. Accrued unpaid 4,000.

decisions.question: Classify Office payroll.
decisions.answer: Administrative operating expense of 96,000 (includes the former finance manager). Accrued unpaid 8,000.

decisions.question: Classify Rent.
decisions.answer: Administrative operating expense of 48,000. No lease agreement is evidenced to support a right-of-use asset.

decisions.question: Classify Marketing.
decisions.answer: Selling and marketing operating expense of 55,000. The photo booth is excluded (capitalised, D044) and so is the villa (distribution, D046).

decisions.question: Classify Software.
decisions.answer: Administrative operating expense of 16,000 (subscriptions, not intangible assets).

decisions.question: Classify Utilities.
decisions.answer: Administrative operating expense of 12,000.

decisions.question: Classify Depreciation.
decisions.answer: Operating expense (non-cash) of 24,000; accumulated depreciation rises from 45,000 to 69,000. Added back in the indirect cash flow.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: management's zero (not booked). Rejected because depreciation is required once assets are in use. A second alternative was to recompute it. There are no useful lives, so a check is only indicative: opening assets of 180,000 over roughly 10 years for 8 months is about 12,000, plus 80,000 of new assets over roughly 5 years for 3.7 months is about 4,900, giving roughly 17,000. 24,000 is plausible with shorter lives. The independent schedule is accepted as the best available evidence.

decisions.question: Classify Bad receivable.
decisions.answer: Bad debt expense of 18,000 (R-17 written off against receivables). This is an adjusting post-period event.
evidence: 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternative 1: a non-adjusting event, because the notice arrived on 3 Sep. Rejected: liquidation existed at 31 Aug and the notice confirms that condition. Alternative 2: R-17 is an additional receivable on top of CRM open items (gross AR 204,000). Rejected: the CRM WEB-NCB line says '€53k gross open; see R-17', and the AR roll-forward ties exactly at 186,000 gross.

decisions.question: Classify Damaged stock.
decisions.answer: Inventory write-down to NRV of 0: a 22,000 expense (shown separately in opex; could be presented within cost of sales).
evidence: 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternative: the founder's 'if it exists it is inventory'. Rejected: IAS 2 lower of cost and NRV, and the independent assessment says it is unsaleable. Considered writing down to minus 2,000 (disposal cost). Rejected: inventory cannot be negative, and any disposal cost is a separate provision question (D072).

decisions.question: Classify Probable legal claim.
decisions.answer: Provision (liability) with a legal or employee expense of 25,000.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternative: disclose it as a contingent liability only (management omitted it). Rejected: counsel says the claim is probable and gives a reliable estimate at the reporting date, so all IAS 37 recognition criteria are met.

decisions.question: Classify Insurance consumed.
decisions.answer: None is recorded: no insurance evidence exists (no payment, policy or prepayment). If a policy is later found, the consumed portion would be opex and any unexpired portion a prepayment. Flagged as a gap and a risk.

decisions.question: Classify Unpaid interest.
decisions.answer: Current liability, interest payable (accrued interest) of 2,000 (12,000 expense - 10,000 paid), confirmed by the bank.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf

decisions.question: Classify Unpaid payroll.
decisions.answer: Current liability, accrued payroll of 32,000 (15,000 opening + 248,000 - 231,000).

decisions.question: Classify Unpaid suppliers.
decisions.answer: Current liability, trade payables of 126,000 (supplier-confirmed).

decisions.answer: Revenue of 180,000 recognised on 12 Feb (signed acceptance). Cash received 180,000; trade receivable 0 at 31 Aug. Management also included it at the invoice amount, so there is no change.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: an unrelated receipt, because bank says 'N STAR' and the CRM spells the customer three ways. Rejected: the amount and date match INV-26012 exactly. It is recognised by management too, so there is no adjustment.

decisions.question: Classify Delivered Freedom contract.
decisions.answer: Revenue of 200,000 recognised on 18 Mar (acceptance). Cash received 142,000; trade receivable 58,000 at 31 Aug. Management also included it at the invoice amount, so there is no change.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: recognise only the cash received (142,000), per management's 'cash received means sold' logic, or hold back revenue until paid. Rejected: control passed on acceptance on 18 Mar, and the 58,000 unpaid is a collectability question. There is no dispute or insolvency evidence, but it is aged over 5 months and should be monitored.

decisions.question: Classify Completed Phoenix event.
decisions.answer: Revenue of 100,000 recognised on 29 Apr (customer email acceptance). Cash received 70,000; trade receivable 30,000 at 31 Aug. Management also included it at the invoice amount, so there is no change.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: defer revenue because final acceptance is only an email (weaker evidence). Rejected: the event was completed on 29 Apr and the customer has paid 70% (bank). The service was delivered, so revenue is recognised in full. Medium-high confidence.

decisions.question: Classify Delivered Liberty order.
decisions.answer: Revenue of 120,000 recognised on 20 Jun (delivery and written acceptance). Cash received 95,000; trade receivable 25,000 at 31 Aug. Management also included it at the invoice amount, so there is no change.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: split the mixed order or treat the glitter complaint as a return risk. Rejected: the customer wrote 'Accepted in full', and there is no return provision evidence.

decisions.question: Classify Undelivered September events.
decisions.answer: Not revenue in the period. These are contract liabilities of 90,000 until delivery on 15 and 24 Sep. Any related costs incurred so far would be inventory or contract costs; none are evidenced.
evidence: 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.challenge: Same economic adjustment as D041 (not additive). Considered a bill-and-hold style argument or recognising revenue proportionally to planning effort. Rejected: there is no delivery, no acceptance, and no evidence of progress towards satisfying the performance obligation.

decisions.question: Classify Loan principal payment.
decisions.answer: Financing cash outflow of 19,000; reduces the loan liability (no P&L effect).
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf

decisions.question: Classify Equipment purchase.
decisions.answer: Investing cash outflow of 80,000 (Pack-O-Matic 60,000 + photo booth 20,000), capitalised as PPE. The 10,000 repair is operating, not investing.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing bad-debt allowance/write-off and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Specific write-off of 18,000 (R-17), with no general allowance. Net AR 168,000 = 58,000 Freedom + 30,000 Phoenix + 25,000 Liberty + 20,000 Stripe FSB + 35,000 WEB-NCB other.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: add a general or expected-credit-loss allowance on the aged Freedom (58,000, over 5 months) and Phoenix (30,000, 4 months) balances. Considered, because collection history is weak (only 70-80% paid). Not booked: no dispute, insolvency or default evidence exists for those customers, so an allowance would be invented. It is disclosed as an uncertainty range of 0 to 88,000 further exposure. Same adjustment as D057 (not additive).

decisions.question: Estimate Damaged inventory write-off and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 22,000: the full carrying value of basement stock, per the independent assessment (no saleable value). The 2,000 disposal cost is not provided for; it is disclosed.
decisions.challenge: Strongest alternative: provide an additional 2,000 disposal cost (total charge 24,000), because the quote relates to stock damaged before 31 Aug. Rejected as the base case: under IAS 37 there was no legal or constructive obligation to dispose at 31 Aug. The disposal is a post-takeover management decision and a future operating cost. NRV cannot take inventory below zero. It is a 2,000 profit risk if the auditor disagrees; low materiality. Same adjustment as D058 (not additive).

decisions.question: Estimate Legal provision and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 25,000: counsel's best estimate (range 20,000-30,000). The range is disclosed.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternatives: the range bottom (20,000, optimistic) or top (30,000, prudent). Rejected: IAS 37 uses the best estimate of the single most likely outcome, and counsel gives 25,000 explicitly. The ±5,000 is disclosed. Same adjustment as D059 (not additive).

decisions.question: Estimate Period depreciation and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 24,000 per the independent depreciation schedule, covering opening PPE (180,000) plus Pack-O-Matic and photo booth from 10 May. Closing accumulated depreciation is 69,000.
decisions.challenge: Alternative: compute depreciation from assumed lives, e.g. about 17,000 using 10-year and 5-year lives. Rejected: no useful-life or residual evidence exists, so a self-computed figure would be less supported than the independent schedule. If the repair had been capitalised, depreciation would change slightly; it is not capitalised. Uncertainty range is roughly 17,000-24,000. Same adjustment as D056 (not additive).

decisions.question: Estimate Closing inventory and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 112,000 = opening 80,000 + purchases 459,000 - COGS 405,000 - damaged write-off 22,000. Versus management's 143,000.
decisions.challenge: Strongest alternative: 121,000 = physical count of good stock (79,000 + 42,000) at system value, excluding the damaged 22,000. Marta's count is recent, independent warehouse evidence, and this would cut COGS to 396,000 (+9,000 profit). Rejected as the base case: the count confirms quantities but values them at the system cost, which 'was not updated'. The 405,000 consumption is tied to valid delivered sales, and 459,000 purchases are third-party invoices. The 9,000 gap is left unreconciled and flagged for investigation. The effect against management's 143,000 is -31,000 (22,000 damaged + 9,000 roll-forward difference); the 22,000 overlaps with D058.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing receivables and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Gross 186,000 (Freedom 58,000, Phoenix 30,000, Liberty 25,000, Stripe FSB 20,000, WEB-NCB 53,000) less R-17 18,000 = 168,000 net. Roll-forward: 35,000 + 960,000 - 809,000 - 18,000 = 168,000. Management's 186,000 excludes the bad debt.

decisions.question: Estimate Repair versus improvement amount and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Repair (expense) 10,000; improvement 0. Invoice R-771 says the work restored normal output with no capacity or life increase. The 60,000 Pack-O-Matic and 20,000 booth are new assets, not improvements.

decisions.question: Estimate Insurance expense and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 0 recorded, because no insurance evidence exists in the bank export or any other file. No amount is estimated or invented. Disclose it as an information gap and a possible uninsured risk.

decisions.question: Estimate Interest payable and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 2,000 = 0 opening + 12,000 expense (loan schedule) - 10,000 paid (bank). Agrees with the bank confirmation of 2,000 accrued unpaid interest.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf

decisions.question: Estimate Accrued payroll and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 32,000 = 15,000 opening + 248,000 expense - 231,000 paid (event 5,000 + sales 4,000 + office 8,000 = 17,000 increase). The founder bonus is excluded.

decisions.question: Estimate Customer deposit liability and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 90,000 = NB-SEP 60,000 + FF-SEP 30,000, received 28-29 Aug for September delivery.

decisions.question: Estimate PPE closing cost and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 260,000 = 180,000 opening + 60,000 Pack-O-Matic + 20,000 photo booth. The 10,000 repair is excluded.

decisions.question: Estimate Accumulated depreciation and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 69,000 = 45,000 opening + 24,000 period charge. Net book value 191,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Supplier payable and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 126,000 = BoxWorks 25,000 + Glass & Drama 28,000 + Print Again 14,000 + Event Things 59,000 (independently confirmed). Roll-forward: 45,000 + 459,000 - 378,000 = 126,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing loan and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 131,000 = 100,000 + 50,000 - 19,000, agreed to the bank confirmation. Current/non-current split not evidenced.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf

decisions.question: Estimate Physical COGS and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 405,000: physical product materials consumed on valid delivered sales (warehouse/purchase reconciliation). The damaged stock of 22,000 is a separate write-off. Alternative on a count basis: 396,000 (see D075).

decisions.question: Estimate Service direct payroll and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 80,000 event delivery staff expense (cash 75,000), charged to cost of sales for Divorce Victory Party events.

decisions.question: Estimate Owner distributions and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 110,000 = villa 70,000 + owner card 40,000 (the same money labelled 'founder bonus'). Charged to equity; financing outflow.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf

decisions.question: Estimate Net profit and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 65,000 = revenue 960,000 - COGS 405,000 - event staff 80,000 (gross profit 475,000) - opex 398,000 (payroll 168,000, rent 48,000, marketing 55,000, software 16,000, utilities 12,000, repairs 10,000, depreciation 24,000, bad debt 18,000, stock write-off 22,000, legal provision 25,000) - interest 12,000. Range about 56,000-80,000 (see uncertainties). Management's 312,000 is rejected.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf

decisions.question: Estimate Closing cash and document the basis.
decisions.answer: 60,000: bank export = bank confirmation = cash-flow roll-forward (80,000 + operating 139,000 - investing 80,000 - financing 79,000). Of this, 90,000 of receipts are customer deposits for undelivered September work; without them cash would have been negative 30,000.

decisions.question: Approve corrected accounts before valuation
decisions.answer: Yes. The board should adopt the corrected accounts (profit 65,000; cash 60,000; equity 125,000; liabilities 406,000) as the only basis for valuation, earn-out and financing discussions, and withdraw the management deck (profit 312,000, cash 186,000).
decisions.challenge: Alternative: wait for a full audit before adopting any figures. Partly accepted: an audit should follow. But the corrections rest on bank, third-party and counsel evidence, and relying on management's figures meanwhile is worse. Asset effect covers the identified management lines only (cash -126,000, AR -18,000, inventory -31,000). Management's liabilities and equity were never presented, so they are not quantified.

decisions.question: Freeze owner-card access
decisions.answer: Yes, immediately. 110,000 of owner spending (villa 70,000 + card 40,000) went through company accounts with no business purpose. Cancel the cards, require dual authorisation, and consider a recovery claim against the founder.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf

decisions.question: Move September deposits to contract liabilities
decisions.answer: Yes. Reclassify 90,000 from revenue to contract liabilities, and recognise revenue on delivery on 15 and 24 Sep. Ensure delivery happens; the cash is already committed to those events.

decisions.question: Begin weekly 13-week cash forecast
decisions.answer: Yes. Cash is 60,000 against 126,000 supplier payables, 32,000 unpaid wages, 2,000 interest, a 25,000 legal claim and 90,000 of deposits whose events must still be delivered. Current liabilities (275,000) exceed cash plus AR (228,000), and the business burned 20,000 even with 90,000 of deposits and 50,000 of new debt. This is a solvency and liquidity warning.

decisions.question: Stop credit sales to insolvent/high-risk customers
decisions.answer: Yes. R-17 cost 18,000, and 113,000 of B2B invoices remain partly unpaid (Freedom 58,000, Phoenix 30,000, Liberty 25,000). Introduce credit checks, deposits and payment terms, and chase aged balances.

decisions.question: Dispose of damaged stock
decisions.answer: Yes. Dispose of it at the quoted cost of about 2,000 (a post-period cost, not provided at 31 Aug). Fix the leaking pipe, and check insurance cover (none evidenced).

decisions.question: Investigate management override and duplicate sources
decisions.answer: Yes. Documented overrides include deposits booked as sales, the loan booked as income, the villa relabelled as marketing then bonus, the omitted legal claim, the retained bad debt and damaged stock, and a 126,000 cash overstatement. Investigate the 9,000 inventory count/book gap and the 45,000 Event Things payment for pre-2026 invoices. Preserve the email and WhatsApp records.
evidence: 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf

decisions.question: Renegotiate supplier terms
decisions.answer: Yes. 126,000 is owed to suppliers against 60,000 cash, and Event Things (59,000) is the largest. Agree payment plans or extended terms to avoid a supply disruption for the September events.

decisions.question: Continue core Finally Single and event operations
decisions.answer: Yes, conditionally. Delivered revenue is real (960,000; gross margin about 49%) and operating cash flow is positive (139,000, though flattered by 90,000 of deposits). Finally Single web sales are the largest, best-collected line. Continue while imposing cash controls. Review the Never Call Back web channel, which has poor collection (37,000 of 90,000) and the R-17 loss.

decisions.question: Use claimed management profit for earn-out
decisions.answer: No. Management profit of 312,000 includes 90,000 of undelivered deposits and 50,000 of loan proceeds, and omits costs. Corrected profit is 65,000. Any earn-out must use the corrected, evidence-based accounts; consider a clawback for the 110,000 of distributions.
evidence: 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
decisions.challenge: Alternative: use management profit adjusted only for the two obvious items (312,000 - 90,000 - 50,000 = 172,000). Rejected: that still omits 107,000 of net cost corrections (bad debt, write-off, legal, depreciation, payroll accrual, reclassifications). The evidence file also contains an embedded instruction to report 312,000, which was deliberately not followed.
